## 4. HAB-01 local dates, cadence and every result producer

### 4.1 Current evidence versus target

dateKeys uses public localDateKey despite the legacy utcDateKey name. computeStreak walks calendar days ending today without schedule/startDate. computeStats uses month/year prefixes; AC-STAT-5 includes December 25 at a May 23 reference. HabitDetail independently implements countForMonth, aggregateMonthCount and elapsed-day denominators for HabitStatsView and AllHabitsView. HabitList today/week summaries, row/single cumulative counts, directory totals, heatmap levels, rankings, progress widths and remaining counts also need the same population contract. No rendered failure or runtime result is claimed by this inspection.

Proposed package-local model, no persisted schema change for decided daily schedules:
- DayKey is a strict existing civil-date string; Today is one sampled local clock snapshot for a render/operation. Parse with the public calendar-date contract, never reinterpret historical strings as UTC instants.
- classifyDay(habit, dayKey, todayKey) returns invalid, before-start, future, rest, due-today, due-past or unresolved-policy. checked is a separate boolean; today-unchecked is pending today, not a past missed day.
- Valid explicit startDate is inclusive; weekdays means Monday–Friday and weekends Saturday–Sunday. Missing legacy frequency retains the existing daily behavior; missing legacy startDate adds no invented lower bound, including no createdAt-derived migration. Invalid/unknown explicit values return unresolved/invalid source, not a silent daily default. Repairing their validator is separately gated.
- eligibleDays(habit, window, today) enumerates civil calendar days in the requested month/week/range, on/after explicit startDate and on/before today, matching the resolved cadence. Historical months end at their actual last day; current month ends at today; future months have no earned opportunity. Dates iterate by civil arithmetic, not 86,400,000 milliseconds.
- completedDays is the set intersection of eligibleDays with valid true check-ins; duplicate or malformed keys and false values do not increase it. Existing non-eligible historical bytes are retained and can be disclosed as excluded records; projection must not erase them.

For resolved schedules, summary returns {eligibleCount, completedCount, rate, remaining, unresolvedHabitIds}. rate = round(100 × completedCount / eligibleCount) with display bounding 0..100, remaining = max(0, eligibleCount - completedCount). Zero eligibleCount produces no completion percentage (display “No due days / 无应完成日”), and zero progress geometry; it never divides by zero or implies 100%. Bounding is defense after a correct set intersection, not a cure for a wrong denominator. All aggregate rates sum eligible/completed opportunities across habits, then divide; they do not average rounded habit rates or divide by all habits × calendar days. A weekly-unresolved member makes the whole aggregate explicitly incomplete; it cannot silently disappear from an “All habits” claim.

E1 annual progress stays year-scoped with the accepted 365/366 calendar-year denominator and its honest annual-progress label; it is not silently converted to an elapsed-month completion rate. Its earned numerator excludes future, before-start and off-schedule records; its remaining count and width stay nonnegative/bounded. Monthly due-cycle percentages use the opportunity denominator above. Total/row cumulative counts and all year/month/ranking/heatmap numerators use only eligible checks through today, with explicit date-range labels. Neither an all-time count nor a heatmap may let future keys inflate achievement.

## 5. HAB-02 source health, day refresh and month following

Current source seeds on meta.isDefault OR habits.length === 0. validateHabitsState collapses invalid shapes to a default and does not establish health. Existing tests expecting corruption/schema-mismatch seeding are old oracles; the new T10 requirement preserves raw corrupt bytes and forbids silent reseeding.

Proposed read boundary: {binding, health: absent|valid|invalid|unavailable, rawBytes, validatedValue?, error?}. A valid empty schema-1 collection is valid, even with zero habits. Truly absent, successfully read, correctly owned source may enter first-launch seed once under admitted writer coordination. Valid empty opens an honest empty UI and issues zero sample writes on render/reopen. Invalid/unknown schema/malformed members retains exact raw bytes, shows recovery/export/reset choices with no automatic replacement; unavailable read retains error and does not infer absence. No initializing fallback may write because a convenience selector returned an empty array. This needs exact validator/storage-source impact review before its implementation if public metadata cannot establish the distinction.

State machine: READ → ABSENT / VALID / INVALID / UNAVAILABLE; only owned ABSENT → authorized SEED_PENDING → VALID on verified success. Failure remains recoverable, does not select fictitious seed records. Explicit clear → verified valid-empty → repeated remount valid-empty. Clear failure preserves old bytes and latest intent. Deletion/tombstone/locked-account is never treated as first launch; reseeding must not resurrect deleted data.

HabitsModule should consume the public accepted local-day clock once and pass one snapshot to its descendants. Midnight, visible/focus/pageshow recovery and calibration resample the real clock, including backward jumps/timezone changes; no write is caused solely by clock render. Existing historical keys and absolute createdAt remain byte-stable. Month state becomes {mode: follow-current|explicit, displayedMonth}. Initial current month follows local month rollover; user prev/next/manual historical navigation enters explicit mode and remains there across midnight. An explicit Today action returns to follow-current. An automatic follow does not steal focus or rewrite selected date/history.

The editor carries its own {owner, generation, habitId, monthKey, editorSession, editSeq}; it does not derive identity anew after month state changes. A dirty/pending/conflicted old-month diary pins the editing month with visible “today changed” feedback until journal-safe navigation/recovery; other today badges may update. Once settled and navigation is permitted, follow-current may advance. Switching habit retains the previous diary under its old identity before initializing the new habit's current-month view. Programmatic host navigation and remount must recover journal identity, not reinterpret old text as the new month.

## 6. HAB-03 per-change durable diary, serialization and lifecycle proposal

### 6.1 Guarantee and concrete design candidate

Current DiaryCard calls onDraftChange per edit but latest text lives in React/ref memory. HabitsModule flushes on selected in-module actions, and usePersistedHabits has a raw baseline comparison. This preserves mounted work in the historical accepted slice; it cannot provide actual close survival or cross-tab atomicity.

Propose a two-stage design for separate storage/lifecycle impact review: synchronous per-change, owner-scoped immutable draft records, followed by serialized canonical commit through an admitted public storage mutation API. This is a concrete technical proposal, not an authorized new store. It deliberately requires a new journal-family/lifecycle grant; silently editing xai_habits_state schema or using an unregistered localStorage key is forbidden.

Proposed record fields: version, ownerId, generation, scopeEpoch, habitId, monthKey, editorSessionId, monotonically increasing editSeq, baseRaw or lossless base identity plus recoverable base bytes, text (including empty deletion intent), recordedAt, canonicalOutcome and acknowledgedSeq. Proposed key identity is the tuple (ownerId,generation,habitId,monthKey,editorSessionId,editSeq), with a separately reviewed physical-key encoding. Distinct tabs/sessions never overwrite one another's journal record. A single global “latest draft” key or timestamp last-writer-wins selector is insufficient. Exact key naming, ownership registration, schema validator, encryption/privacy classification and physical storage limits are deliverables of that impact phase, not existing APIs.

On every user change, capture the fixed editor identity and latest full text; attempt the synchronous journal write and strict readback before the change is labelled durably retained. No debounce before durable storage; a later canonical debounce is allowed only after every current edit has its own verified journal record. Acknowledgement is an observation of the per-change write, not permission to exclude “just typed but unacknowledged” input from the healthy-storage direct-close acceptance. Actual type-immediate-close-before-blur must recover the final text without waiting for a timer or Save button.

If quota/access/readback fails, keep the exact latest input visible, show Not durably saved with error, retain earlier durable records and allow retry/export; never report Saved. Faulted close cannot be counted as a durability PASS for lost latest text, and the implementation may not promise storage guarantees the platform did not provide. An uncertain readback might have written bytes: preserve both candidate and previous evidence; retry verifies identity and intended bytes before publishing acknowledgement. No rollback that destroys unknown newer bytes. If this candidate cannot satisfy the healthy latest-input guarantee and safe owner lifecycle together, HAB-03 stays blocked for revised technical design within its remaining contract budget, not a weakened product promise.

### 6.2 Canonical state and APIs (proposed signatures)

- captureDiaryBinding() returns immutable account owner/generation/epoch plus editorSession; locked/unresolved ownership refuses a writable editor.
- stageDiaryEdit(binding, habitId, monthKey, seq, text, base) returns durable(recordId, seq) | failed(error, uncertain). It never retargets the tuple to a later account or month.
- commitDiary(recordId, expectedBase) returns committed(revision/rawIdentity, seq) | conflict(externalRaw, recordId) | refused(reason) | failed(error, uncertain).
- recoverDiary(binding) returns all applicable durable records grouped by habit/month/session with latest per-session sequence, plus current canonical source and health. No automatic choice between divergent sessions.
- retry(recordId), exportRecovery(recordId), discard(recordId) retain the captured binding and explicit action attribution. Discard is a coordinated tombstone/cleanup operation, not a text reset that can later resurrect an old draft.

Editor states: clean → journal-pending (synchronous boundary) → durable-draft → canonical-pending → saved. Any stage may become write-failed, source-invalid, source-unavailable, owner-stale or conflict. New edit N+1 stays the visible value while N completes. Only verified N+1 canonical success marks current input Saved; N success can mark its own record committed but never clear N+1. Canonical queue coalesces only after preserving all latest durable values, at most one active mutation per binding/key; failure stops automatic busy retries. First-edit baseline survives retries. No unload/blur callback is necessary for journal survival; these may request canonical flushing but are not the guarantee.

### 6.3 Two documents, refusal, recovery and generation

Commit must hold the existing admitted account shared lock then the canonical-key exclusive lock, recheck owner/generation/epoch/tombstone/source health and expected raw baseline inside the critical section, produce the next full valid blob without deleting unrelated fields, write/read back, and publish success exactly once. If locking/admission is unavailable or legacy writers remain unclassified, refuse canonical commit; do not fall back to compare-then-set and claim atomicity. D2 supports only participating converted writers. Grant requires an actual writer census and coexistence plan for create/check-in/seed/diary/migration/delete, not only conversion of one textarea.

A two-tab barrier fixture must force both documents to capture one base, then serialize: first canonical writer commits; second refuses with conflict and preserves its durable text plus exact newer external bytes. StorageEvent is only a notification to re-read the physical binding; payload is not the source of truth. Clean readers adopt validated source. Dirty/durable/pending readers retain their draft and original base, show conflict, and never “retry” by quietly adopting a new base. Explicit reload/discard can adopt external state only after the local durable record is safely exported or explicitly discarded; export offers both raw external and local draft with tuple/sequence. Independent later changes while the recovery UI is open invalidate a stale action again.

A→B, locked state, A→B→A and same-account new generation invalidate old callbacks and queue admission. A's text must not be shown/exported/committed under B. A durable record stays in A's proper generation for lawful recovery/export, not copied into the active account. Returning to A opens a new session and explicitly discovers applicable records; stale promise completions cannot mark it Saved. Migration must account for staged journals before publishing a new generation; an old-generation edit waiting behind exclusive migration refuses instead of stranding a false success. Deletion acquires lifecycle authority, tombstones/invalidate writers, removes canonical and journal-family data, and proves stale callbacks cannot recreate either. Export includes current-generation journal data with honest omissions; uncertain/mixed-owner archives remain intact device-local and not misclassified. These are required impact acceptance rows, with no new lifecycle writer grant here.

Host AppRail/programmatic route/Back/Forward/sign-out/feature-disable/host unmount must be evaluated through actual production composition in a future frozen task. Durable journal prevents data loss; any unsaved-navigation/coordinator seam still needs separate impact review. In-memory unmount tests and legacy ConsoleLayout are insufficient substitutes.

## 8. HAB-05 truthful preferences, permissions and scheduling

Current AddHabitDialog defaults reminderEnabled=true and persists enabled/time. The saved display is HabitsListView in HabitDetail, not AllHabitsView. types delegates scheduling to future notification work. Settings push_habit is a distinct preference. Inspected /sw.js install/activate/fetch behavior is no scheduled-delivery evidence; this is a bounded source observation, not a repository-wide or live-platform proof.

Proposed UI state is a product of independent dimensions:
- preference: off | editing | saving | saved | save-failed, from actual persistence result;
- capability: unknown | unsupported | available, from a truthful read-only capability boundary;
- permission: unknown | default | denied | granted, from actual platform observation when available;
- schedule: unavailable | not-requested | pending | acknowledged | refused | cancelled | stale, only backed by a matching current job receipt.

Default new reminder preference off until the scheduling product is available; preserve existing saved enabled/time values as preferences and label “Preference saved; reminders not scheduled / 偏好已保存；提醒尚未安排”. Unsupported/default/denied/granted must remain distinct. Permission granted does not imply schedule acknowledged; saved does not imply delivery. A read error is unknown, never supported/granted. Do not prompt permission on mount or saving a preference. An explicit user request/test notification, if later granted, reports only its actual immediate delivery result and never “scheduled”. Current bounded scope may render schedule unavailable; no positive scheduled claim is legal without actual matching JOB identity.

Future scheduling receipt contract belongs to JOB: owner/generation, habit identity, jobId/revision, idempotency key, intended local recurrence/timezone and resolved dueAt, permission observation, scheduling acknowledgement, cancellation/replacement and delivery outcome. Reminder edits require stale receipt invalidation and idempotent replacement; permission loss, offline retry, owner change/deletion, DST and duplicate execution have their own JOB oracles. Closed-page/browser-closed delivery needs actual external job/delivery evidence; a page timer, service-worker registration, saved HH:mm or one-shot Notification is insufficient. Calendar jobs, account-sync and host/SW writers remain locked. No JOB implementation budget is assigned here.
